    • Precision Weighting with curveRweights

Estimate precision weights from a curveR calibration result

Source: R/fit_precision_weights.R
fit_precision_weights.Rd

The curveR-ecosystem entry point. Two models are available.

Usage

fit_precision_weights(
  data,
  design = NULL,
  scale_predictor = c("se", "pcov"),
  plate_col = NULL,
  patient_col = NULL,
  model = c("multiplicative", "additive"),
  use_censoring = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Either the output of as_weight_data() (class weight_data), or a calibration_result(_multiplate) / plain data.frame, in which case design is required and as_weight_data() is called internally.

design

Character vector of design-group columns (required unless data is already a weight_data).

scale_predictor

Multiplicative model only: "se" (default; uncapped log10-scale SD) or "pcov" (legacy, lossy because of the cap). The additive model always uses se.

plate_col

Plate grouping column for the location random intercept. Defaults to "curve_id" when present, else NULL.

patient_col

Subject column for the subject random intercept (additive model). Defaults to "patientid" when present, else NULL.

model

"multiplicative" (default, 0.2.x behaviour) or "additive" (recommended; see Description).

use_censoring

Additive model: use the censoring columns (censor_type, censor_lower, censor_upper) when the data carry them. Default TRUE. If dilution is also present the response is placed on the final-concentration scale, which is the scale of curveRcore's bounds.

...

MCMC controls and priors passed to fit_additive_weight() or fit_saturated_weight() (e.g. iter, warmup, chains, cores, adapt_delta, seed; fix_beta1 for the additive model).

Value

A precision_weights object: a list with $estimates, $weights, $design, $scale, and $fit.

For the additive model $estimates holds tau, tau2, kappa, beta1, their intervals, the overall reliability, and diagnostics; $weights (keyed by obs_id/sampleid/curve_id) has se, pcov, v_meas, tau2, sigma (total), w, reliability, reliability_lo/hi, w_norm, censor_type and bound. See compute_additive_weights() for what each column is for. For the multiplicative model $estimates holds phi, beta1 and $weights has se, pcov, sigma, w, w_norm.

Details

model = "multiplicative" (the default, unchanged from 0.2.x so that existing callers such as the i-spi-compute worker keep working) fits \(\sigma_i = \phi\, se_i^{\beta_1}\) (fit_saturated_weight()). It attributes all variance to the measurement, so very precisely measured samples can receive extreme weights.

model = "additive" (recommended for new analyses) fits the measurement-error model of fit_additive_weight(): \(\sigma_i^2 = \tau^2 + \kappa^2 se_i^{2\beta_1}\), which separates true between-subject variance (\(\tau^2\)) from measurement error and yields weights \(w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2\) that are bounded above by \(1/\tau^2\), a per-observation reliability, and a censored likelihood for samples outside the quantifiable range. The additive result has a different $estimates shape (tau, kappa, reliability instead of phi); callers must opt in knowingly.

See also

as_weight_data(), predict_weights(), join_weights(), fit_additive_weight(), fit_saturated_weight()

# wd <- as_weight_data(mp, design = c("timeperiod", "cohort_arm"))
# pw <- fit_precision_weights(wd, iter = 1000, warmup = 500, chains = 2)
# pw$estimates$tau2; pw$estimates$reliability
# }
